title: Unramified characters bijection X^ur(G) ↔ Cosh_G(B(G); 1_Fix) (App B.1)
body_html:
$\mathcal{X}^{\mathrm{ur}}(G)$ bijects with isomorphism classes in $\Cosh_G(\mathcal{B}(G); \mathbf{1}_{\mathrm{Fix}})$

Let $\mathcal{X}^{\mathrm{ur}}(G)$ be the set of unramified characters of $G(F)$, and $\Cosh_G(\mathcal{B}(G); \mathbf{1}_{\mathrm{Fix}})$ the subcategory of cosheaves on $\mathcal{B}(G)$ such that $\mathscr{V}_E$ is trivial as a representation and $\Fix_G(E)$ acts trivially.

A character $\chi$ gives the cosheaf with $\mathscr{V}_E = R$, identity restrictions, and equivariance $a_{g, E} = \chi(g) \cdot$.

Proposition. This map is a bijection of $\mathcal{X}^{\mathrm{ur}}(G)$ with isomorphism classes of $\Cosh_G(\mathcal{B}(G); \mathbf{1}_{\mathrm{Fix}})$.
proof_html:
Injectivity is straightforward. Surjectivity: for any $\mathscr{V}$ in this category, $H_i(C_\bullet \mathscr{V}) = 0$ for $i > 0$ and $H_0(C_\bullet \mathscr{V}) = R$. The induced $G$-action on $H_0$ is by a character $\chi$. For each vertex $x$, $\mathscr{V}x \to H_0(\mathscr{V})$ is $\Fix_G(x)$-equivariant, so $\chi|{\Fix_G(x)}$ is trivial; since $\bigcup_x \Fix_G(x) = G^1(k)$, $\chi|_{G^1(k)} = 1$, i.e. $\chi$ is unramified. $\square$

This justifies the Remark in Heisenberg–Weil equivalence Cosh_G(X,phi) ≃ Cosh_G(X,1_{QJ}) (Prop 4.2) that $\Cosh_G(X, \mathbf{1}_{QJ})$ is equivalent to the category of unramified characters when $Q_E = \Fix_G(E)$.
